growth_stages.name: Germination
growth_stages.description: Seed imbibes water and radicle emerges.

growth_stages.name: Vegetative growth
growth_stages.description: Rapid leaf and stalk growth, highest nutrient demand.

growth_stages.name: Grain filling
growth_stages.description: Kernel development, milk to dough stage.

growth_stages.name: Physiological maturity
growth_stages.description: Black layer formation, ready for harvest.

operations.name: Land Clearing
operations.description: Removal of vegetation/debris from the plot.

operations.name: Pest & Disease Scouting/Control
operations.description: Fall armyworm and other pest management.

operations.name: Harvest (Fresh/Green Cob)
operations.description: NEW operation, added per the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset: harvesting for fresh/green eating corn at the milk-to-dough stage, distinct from letting the crop mature to dry grain. The previous version of this file only modeled dry grain harvest, conflating two genuinely different farmer decisions into one operation.

operations.name: Harvest (Dry Grain)
operations.description: Dry grain harvesting at physiological maturity.

operations.name: Drying
operations.description: Field or platform drying to safe moisture content.

validation_rules.condition: Land preparation cannot be logged before land clearing, and should not be logged more than 30 days after it.

CORRECTED per the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset: planting before land preparation is a hard block, but that case is already caught by the global backdate rule (maize_r11), since land preparation would be the most recently logged operation. This rule's own severity should therefore be warning, for the case of planting more than 30 days after land preparation (soil loses tilth/moisture advantage), not a block at 14 days as the previous version incorrectly stated.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026 -- supersedes the earlier self-sourced 14-day figure

validation_rules.condition: Basal NPK (e.g. 15:15:15) should be applied at planting or within the first 1-2 weeks after planting.
validation_rules.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020; corroborated by Seed Co Nigeria agronomic guidance

validation_rules.condition: The critical weed-free window is 14-21 days after planting; logged outside that but still at or after 7 days is flagged. See maize_r4_floor for the separate hard block under 7 days.
validation_rules.source: Farmwarehouse / IITA extension guidance, Step by Step Maize Production in Nigeria; boundary structure corrected against the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, which specifies three tiers here rather than a single warning band

validation_rules.condition: NEW rule, added per the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset: weeding logged before 7 days after planting is a hard block, there is nothing meaningful to weed yet at that point. This floor did not exist in the previous version of this file.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: Base/umbrella typical window, now 21-42 days per the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset (previously 21-35, sourced only from IITA's regional figures). The precise window still differs by zone -- see regional_overrides: Guinea savanna is 28-35 days, Sudan savanna (extra-early varieties) is 21-28 days, both of which sit inside this broader typical window. See maize_r5_floor for the hard block boundary, which did not exist in the previous version of this file.
validation_rules.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020 (regional figures, unchanged); typical window widened to 21-42 per the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: NEW rule: top-dress logged before 14 days or after 60 days after planting is a hard block. The previous version of this file had no hard block at all for this operation, only the warning-severity typical-window rule, meaning an absurdly late top-dress (e.g. day 100) would have passed with only a soft flag.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: Second manual weeding is recommended 4-5 weeks after planting.
validation_rules.source: Farmwarehouse / IITA extension guidance, Step by Step Maize Production in Nigeria

validation_rules.condition: Fall Armyworm control is most effective when insecticide is applied weekly during the first 3 weeks after planting; scouting/control logged well outside this window is flagged since FAW damage compounds quickly if missed early. The Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset frames this differently: it calls for calendar/routine sprays to be blocked entirely, only allowing a spray once scouting confirms 5-10%+ damage. AgTrail's schema does not yet have a field to represent 'evidence of scouting threshold met' as a precondition on an operation, so that specific requirement cannot be enforced yet -- flagged as a real, current limitation rather than silently ignored. See maize_r7_floor for the one piece of that guidance this schema CAN enforce: a hard block on spraying after tasseling.
validation_rules.source: Farmwarehouse, Step by Step Maize Production in Nigeria (Ampligo/Emacot application schedule); evidence-gating principle per the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, not yet enforceable in this schema

validation_rules.condition: NEW rule: pesticide application after tasseling (65 days after planting) is a hard block, this is late enough that FAW spraying is no longer appropriate and the operation likely represents a different pest/disease control action, or a data error. This did not exist in the previous version of this file. Note: operation_id 'pest_scouting' is used generically for all pest and disease control in this file, so this block boundary is specifically about FAW-context sprays per the source ruleset -- it may be too broad if later used for legitimate late-season scouting unrelated to FAW, flagged as a known modeling limitation.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: Harvest cannot be logged before 80 days after planting (physiologically impossible even for the earliest-maturing hybrids). Upper bound CORRECTED from 150 to 160 days per the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset. The 80-day floor is retained from the earlier cross-referenced sources since the master ruleset does not state one explicitly, and is not contradicted by it.
validation_rules.source: Cross-referenced: Ghana MOFA Maize Production Guide, IITA/USAID Nigeria manuals, FAO regional guide (80-day floor, unchanged); upper bound corrected to 160 per the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: 90-130 days covers physiological maturity through the point where loss to birds/rot becomes a real concern. Upper bound CORRECTED from 120 to 130 days per the master ruleset ('flag after 130 DAP'). Harvest logged inside the hard block range (80-160 days) but outside this typical window is flagged so the farmer can confirm their variety's maturity class rather than being blocked outright.
validation_rules.source: IITA maturity-class guidance, Ghana MOFA (90-115 days, unchanged); upper bound corrected to 130 per the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: NEW rule: fresh/green cob harvest cannot be logged before 60 days after planting. No upper block -- past a certain point a late 'fresh' harvest just becomes a de facto dry grain harvest instead, which is covered by the separate harvest operation.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: NEW rule: 65-75 days after planting is the typical milk-to-dough stage window for fresh/green cob harvest. Outside this but past the 60-day floor is flagged rather than blocked.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: Fresh/green cob harvest can only be logged once per planting cycle, same reasoning as dry grain harvest.
Harvest can only be logged once per planting cycle for an annual crop; a second harvest record requires a new planting record first.

Drying should begin promptly after harvest to bring grain to a safe storage moisture content and avoid mold/storage pest (grain weevil) infestation; the field-drying/harvest guidance from Feed the Future's manual notes maize is typically harvested close to physiological maturity and then requires deliberate drying, not left to dry indefinitely on the stalk.
validation_rules.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020 (storage pest section); Feed the Future Manual for Maize Farming

validation_rules.condition: Global rule: no operation may be logged with a date earlier than the previous operation's logged date for the same farm/cycle (no backdating that would reorder the sequence).

weather_preferences.notes: Sensitive to moisture stress during tasseling/silking; waterlogging is harmful at all stages.

diseases.name: Maize Streak Virus
diseases.symptoms: Chlorotic streaking along leaf veins, stunted growth.
diseases.management: Use resistant/tolerant varieties (e.g. ZPBSR, DMR-LSRW streak-resistant hybrids), control leafhopper vectors, plant early with the onset of rains.
diseases.source: IITA / USAID, Growing Maize in Nigeria

diseases.name: Maize Leaf Blight
diseases.management: Crop rotation, resistant varieties, fungicide if severe.
diseases.source: General extension guidance - less specifically documented in the Nigeria-specific sources reviewed so far; flagged for agronomist follow-up

pests.name: Fall Armyworm (FAW)
pests.symptoms: Ragged leaf feeding, sawdust-like frass in the whorl; larvae light green to dark brown with longitudinal stripes.
pests.management: Scout from emergence; approved insecticides (e.g. Ampligo, Emacot) applied once per week for the first 3 weeks after planting are effective in Nigeria. FAW affects 350+ plant species and is one of the most destructive invasive pests in the region.
pests.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020; Farmwarehouse, Step by Step Maize Production in Nigeria

pests.name: Striga (Striga hermonthica)
pests.symptoms: Parasitic weed attaching to maize roots; visible purple-flowered weed emergence, severe stunting and yield loss even before the weed itself is visible above ground.
pests.management: Resistant/tolerant hybrids, crop rotation with non-host (trap) crops, balanced soil fertility (Striga is worse on depleted soils), timely weeding before Striga seed-set.
pests.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020 - noted as a major constraint (up to 74% infestation in the northern Guinea savanna, 30-60% of yield losses attributed to it)

pests.name: Stem Borer
pests.symptoms: Bore holes in stalk, dead heart in young plants.
pests.management: Field sanitation, timely planting, targeted insecticide application.
pests.source: General extension guidance - not yet cross-checked against a Nigeria-specific primary source; flagged for agronomist follow-up

yield_model.notes: 1.2-2.0 t/ha reflects typical unoptimized smallholder yields; 2.5-3.5 t/ha (up to ~3+ t/ha) reflects recommended-practice yields in Northern Nigeria per IITA. Treat the top of this range as achievable-with-good-management rather than typical.

tiers.message: A reported yield of 0 t/ha must be logged as a Disaster/Loss Event, not a harvest record.
Near-total crop failure; verify plot area and inputs.
Exceptional; requires manual review of seed and management.
Approaches the biological limit for rainfed maize -- almost certainly a kg/tonne unit typo or inflated area.

yield_validation.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026. NEW dimension not present in the previous version of this file -- assumes reported area is trustworthy, which depends on GPS-polygon-anchored area tracking that AgTrail does not yet implement (self-reported area could still be gamed to manipulate the resulting t/ha figure even with this check in place).

validation_rules.condition: Nitrogen top-dress (urea) applied 4-5 weeks after planting -- Guinea savanna zone window.
validation_rules.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020

validation_rules.condition: Nitrogen top-dress (urea) applied 3-4 weeks after planting for extra-early varieties -- Sudan savanna zone window (shorter than Guinea savanna because extra-early varieties are typically grown here).
validation_rules.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020

version_history.summary: Initial structured template built from general agronomic references. NOT yet validated by an agronomist - treat all intervals/thresholds as provisional.
version_history.source: Draft / general references (FAO, IITA public guidance) - pending expert review

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - sourced revision pass
version_history.summary: Replaced provisional intervals with numbers cross-checked against named published sources: fertilizer timing (basal 0-14 days, top-dress 21-35 days after planting), weeding schedule (14-21 and 28-35 days), Fall Armyworm spray window (0-21 days), and harvest window split into a hard block range (80-150 days, covering all maturity classes) plus a narrower warning range (90-120 days, typical medium-maturity varieties). Added Striga as a pest entry per IITA's emphasis on it as a major constraint. Every validation_rule and diseases/pests entry now carries a 'source' field. This is still NOT a substitute for an agronomist's sign-off -- it is a materially stronger draft, not a validated final version. Two entries (Maize Leaf Blight, Stem Borer) are explicitly flagged as weaker sources needing follow-up.
version_history.source: IITA - Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria (2020); IITA/USAID - Growing Maize in Nigeria; Farmwarehouse - Step by Step Maize Production in Nigeria; Seed Co Nigeria - Good Agronomic Practices for Maize Farming; Ghana MOFA - Guide to Maize Production; Feed the Future Innovation Lab - Manual for Maize Farming

version_history.summary: Split the second_fertilizer (top-dress) timing rule by region rather than leaving one merged 21-35 day window: IITA's source actually gives Guinea savanna zones 28-35 days and Sudan savanna (extra-early varieties) 21-28 days -- these had been incorrectly averaged into a single range in v1.1.0. Base rule maize_r5 is now documented as a fallback umbrella for when region is unknown; regional_overrides carries the precise per-zone window. This is the first crop file to actually use regional_overrides, so it also establishes the convention: overrides.validation_rules is a list of partial patches keyed by rule_id, applied over the base rule of the same id.
version_history.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - reconciled against the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset
version_history.summary: This is the first genuine agronomist-authored review this file has received, everything before this was self-sourced from public agricultural guides, not verified by a domain expert. Corrections made: (1) maize_r2, planting-after-land-prep changed from an incorrect hard block at 14 days to a warning at 30 days, since the true hard block condition (planting before land prep at all) is already covered by the global backdate rule. (2) maize_r4, added a new hard-block floor at 7 days for first weeding, which had no lower bound at all before. (3) maize_r5, widened the typical top-dress window to 21-42 days and added a genuinely new hard block boundary (14-60 days) that did not exist previously, meaning an absurdly late top-dress used to only get a soft warning, now it is correctly rejected. (4) maize_r7, added a hard block on pesticide application after tasseling (65 days), and documented an honest limitation: the source ruleset also calls for blocking routine calendar sprays in favor of evidence-gated ones (only allowing a spray once scouting confirms 5-10 percent damage), which this schema cannot yet enforce since it has no field for 'scouting evidence threshold met.' (5) Split harvest into two genuinely different operations: harvest_fresh (green/milk-to-dough cob, 60 day floor, 65-75 typical) and the existing harvest (dry grain), which the previous version of this file had conflated into one. (6) Corrected the dry grain harvest bounds: hard block upper bound 150 to 160 days, typical warning upper bound 120 to 130 days. (7) Added an entirely new yield_validation dimension (5-tier structure validating reported harvest tonnes per hectare, independent of timing), which is a new subsystem, not a data correction, and is not yet wired into the validation engine's operation-timing logic. Every changed rule states explicitly what changed and why, rather than silently overwriting the prior sourced values.
version_history.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026
